14:1.sourceText: Μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία· πιστεύετε εἰς τὸν Θεόν, καὶ εἰς ἐμὲ πιστεύετε.
14:1.targetText: “Do not let your heart be troubled, believe in God, believe also in Me;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

14:2.sourceText: ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Πατρός μου μοναὶ πολλαί εἰσιν· εἰ δὲ μή, εἶπον ἂν ὑμῖν· ὅτι πορεύομαι ἑτοιμάσαι τόπον ὑμῖν·
14:2.targetText: in the house of My Father are many rooms; and if not, I would have told you; I go on to prepare a place for you;

groups.note: The Greek aorist told plus counterfactual modal particle is rendered I would have told as a single unreal-result predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has a content/explanatory ὅτι before I go; LSV separates I go as an independent clause without a separate connective.

14:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν πορευθῶ καὶ ἑτοιμάσω τόπον ὑμῖν, πάλιν ἔρχομαι καὶ παραλήμψομαι ὑμᾶς πρὸς ἐμαυτόν, ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἦτε.
14:3.targetText: and if I go on and prepare a place for you, I come again, and will receive you to Myself, that where I am you also may be;

14:4.sourceText: καὶ ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω οἴδατε τὴν ὁδόν.
14:4.targetText: and to where I go away you have known, and the way you have known.”

groups.note: N1904 has one knowing predicate with the way as its object. LSV repeats knowing, first for the destination and then for the way; the actual way-knowing predicate is retained here.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds a separate destination-knowing predicate; N1904 has one knowing predicate governing the way, linked to the final English occurrence.
LSV inserts an additional and before the way-knowing clause, which is not separate in pinned N1904.

14:5.sourceText: Λέγει αὐτῷ Θωμᾶς Κύριε, οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ὑπάγεις· πῶς οἴδαμεν τὴν ὁδὸν;
14:5.targetText: Thomas says to Him, “Lord, we have not known to where You go away, and how are we able to know the way?”

groups.note: N1904 has the finite we know; LSV makes knowing an infinitive under the added are-we-able predicate. The knowing action is shared with that finite-to-infinitive recasting explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds and before how; N1904 begins the next question with how alone.
LSV adds an ability predicate before to know; pinned N1904 simply asks how we know without a separate ability verb.

14:6.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωή· οὐδεὶς ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα εἰ μὴ δι’ ἐμοῦ.
14:6.targetText: Jesus says to him, “I AM the way, and the truth, and the life, no one comes to the Father, if not through Me;

14:7.sourceText: εἰ ἐγνώκειτέ με, καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου ἂν ᾔδειτε· ἀπ’ ἄρτι γινώσκετε αὐτὸν καὶ ἑωράκατε.
14:7.targetText: if you had known Me, you would also have known My Father, and from this time you have known Him, and have seen Him.”

groups.note: The Greek Him is the shared object of knowing and having seen; English repeats Him with both coordinated predicates, so both refer to the one explicit source object.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds and before from this time; N1904 proceeds directly with the time phrase.

14:8.targetText: Philip says to Him, “Lord, show to us the Father, and it is enough for us”;

14:9.targetText: Jesus says to him, “Such [a] long time am I with you, and you have not known Me, Philip? He who has seen Me has seen the Father; and how do you say, Show to us the Father?

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English article supplies a long time; the Greek duration noun is anarthrous.

14:10.sourceText: οὐ πιστεύεις ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί ἐστιν; τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ λαλῶ· ὁ δὲ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ.
14:10.targetText: Do you not believe that I [am] in the Father, and the Father is in Me? The sayings that I speak to you, I do not speak from Myself, and the Father who is abiding in Me does the works Himself;

groups.note: Greek adjectival abiding participle is expanded as the English relative who is abiding; no extra source who or is is written.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness grammatical-role difference: N1904 has possessive αὐτοῦ, His works, while LSV has intensive Himself as the doer. Unlike possessive and intensive pronoun roles are not exchanged.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies the first in-the-Father clause; no Greek copula is written in that first clause.
LSV gives intensive Himself; N1904 instead has genitive αὐτοῦ qualifying works, His works.

14:11.sourceText: πιστεύετέ μοι ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί· εἰ δὲ μή, διὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτὰ πιστεύετε.
14:11.targetText: believe Me, that I [am] in the Father, and the Father in Me; and if not, because of the works themselves, believe Me.

groups.note: The Greek Me specifies the object of the first believe command and is the understood same object of the repeated believe command. LSV repeats Me at both commands; the actual in-Me pronoun is a separate source occurrence.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies I am in the Father; Greek has a nominal in-the-Father clause without a written copula.

14:17.targetText: the Spirit of truth, whom the world is not able to receive, because it does not see nor know [this] One, and you know [this] One, because [this] One remains with you, and will be in you.

groups.note: The neuter personal object pronoun refers to the Spirit; LSV renders it as One. It is the object of seeing/knowing, not the English subject it of the seeing predicate.
Greek remains has the Spirit as its implicit third-person subject; LSV makes that same subject explicit as One remains.
